title: Base-field tangent scalars and canonical structural stalk maps
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ its structure morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $x\in X$. Write $R_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for the structure-ring stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and $\kappa(x)$ for its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Define the structural stalk homomorphism $\sigma_x:k\to R_x$ as the composite of the canonical map from $k$ to its stalk at $s(x)$ with $s_x^\sharp$. Define $\rho_x:k\to\kappa(x)$ by composing $\sigma_x$ with the residue map. The tangent space $T_{X/k,x}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with its canonical $\kappa(x)$-vector-space structure, is regarded as a $k$-vector space by restriction along $\rho_x$: $a\cdot v=\rho_x(a)\cdot v$. For any scheme morphism $f:Y\to Z$, points $y\in Y$, $z\in Z$ and equality $e:f(y)=z$, define the identified stalk homomorphism $\operatorname{stalkMapAt}(f,y,z,e):\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ by transporting the source stalk along $e$ and then applying the usual contravariant stalk map $f_y^\sharp$.
